transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-20 15:00 PDT / Duration: ~48 minutes / Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Ruiz (Astra Head of ML), Tom Bennett (Astra Infra), Sandeep Rao (Astra CTO)

00:00 Jordan: okay all right hey everyone thanks for joining, we know it's a busy week, we'll kick off — this is our weekly POC sync, benchmark review vs baseline provider, stick to 45, 50 ish minutes, and we'll go over the sheets we shared.
00:12 Maya: yep thanks Jordan, appreciate it. we've been looking forward to the perf numbers.
00:18 Priya: quick note, I uploaded the tuned config and the perf scripts into the shared folder, link in chat, there's also a smaller csv with the p50/p95/p99s.
00:27 Tom: saw the link, thanks.
00:30 Jordan: cool. quick agenda: 1) results summary, 2) deep dive on p99 latency cases, 3) tuning knobs (batching/quant/KV cache), 4) security/perf tradeoffs, 5) next steps.
00:40 Sandeep: sounds good.

02:05 Jordan: okay jumping in — high level, across our hosted configs running the 13B open model you guys provided, Redwood with q4-int8 + KV cache delivered median latency about 110ms for single-turn requests at 512 tokens, p95 ~220ms, p99 ~380ms on our dedicated test fleet. Baseline provider reported p50 125ms, p95 240ms, p99 520ms in their email run. so roughly 25% better p99 for us in this workload.
02:40 Maya: those are promising numbers. are these cold-start inclusive?
02:45 Priya: good question — numbers are steady-state, KV cache warmed; cold-start spikes exist but are mitigated with pre-warming and short-lived containers, we have a separate cold-start sheet.
02:54 Tom: the baseline's throughput numbers looked higher on batch sizes >64, they had better sustained throughput, is that right?
03:02 Priya: yes, ProviderX tune favored very large micro-batching which bumps throughput but increases tail latency for small interactive traffic. our approach uses continuous batching and dynamic slice windows to keep latency bounded.

05:15 Jordan: I also want to call out cost per token comparison — on equivalent GPU nodes our unit cost was about 18% lower when accounting for fewer p99 timeouts and less retrying; note these are approximate.
05:26 Maya: can you share the cost model?
05:30 Jordan: yes I'll attach the spreadsheet; it's in the shared drive under benchmarks -> cost_model_redwood_vs_baseline.csv

07:00 Priya: digging into p99 cases — we saw two common patterns: long sequence lengths (1k+ tokens) and request bursts that exhaust the batch window causing queuing. For sequence length heavy requests, quantization plus larger KV shards reduced memory pressure and kept inference on-device. For burst queuing, autoscale and burst capacity mattered.
07:30 Maya: our traffic has a long-tail — about 8% of requests run >1k tokens, so that aligns with what we see in production.
07:38 Priya: for that tail we recommended a mixed routing policy: route long sequences to dedicated heavier instances (pin to d-highmem) and short interactive ones to the low-latency pool. that was in the config doc.
07:47 Tom: when you say quantization, did you use int8 or int4? we worry about quality drift.
07:52 Priya: we tried q4 and q8 (and q3 in a couple experiments). q4-int8 gave best perf/quality balance. we ran the eval suite (the 2000 prompts you provided) — rouge/accuracy delta within noise for q4; for q3 we saw small regressions on some prompt types.
08:10 Maya: that's acceptable if we can flag regression examples.

10:05 Jordan: on the baseline provider notes — there were some infra differences: they used a larger instance type with higher mem-bandwidth which explain their higher throughput on giant batches; they also didn't enable KV cache so their p99 for multi-turn is worse.
10:22 Sandeep: we asked them about their KV approach and they said they kept cache in external redis which added network hop. could that explain the tail?
10:30 Priya: yes, network hop + serialization adds latency variance. our in-runtime KV avoids the hop.

12:40 Maya: latency SLO for our app is p99 < 450ms interactive. looks like Redwood meets that in steady-state but borderline in some long-seq cases. is that fair?
12:50 Jordan: correct, in our runs we were ~380ms p99 for the typical test; for the 1k+ token tail we saw p99 up to 680ms before routing/tuning. with mixed routing we can bring those into 400-450ms range.

15:00 Tom: about reliability — if we route long seq to dedicated, what's the overhead of maintaining dedicated nodes, costs, and cold start risk?
15:10 Priya: you can reserve a small pool (reserved capacity) for long sequences; we also support autoscale with a burst buffer. cost rises but is predictable via Reserved/Dedicated pricing. we'll add a cost/run estimate in the spreadsheet.

18:25 Jordan: QA/Compliance — Maya you had asked about KMS and audit logs? quick update: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and we export audit logs for every inference call in the Private stack, and Hosted has SOC2 controls and rotation.
18:40 Maya: great, for Astra we need HSM-backed keys for PHI in some regions, is that on the roadmap for Private?
18:48 Jordan: yes, HSM integrations available via our enterprise package; I'll include the security whitepaper link.

21:05 Priya: back to perf — we ran an A/B synthetic where we replayed a day of Astra traffic at 2x to stress queueing. Redwood handled burst with auto-batching and dynamic slot expansion; ProviderX started dropping to retries at 2.5x. See the "stress_replay.csv" in the folder.
21:25 Tom: are retries caused by timeouts or OOMs?
21:29 Priya: timeouts due to queue windows hitting thresholds and fallback. We log and trace each retry.

24:00 Maya: can you walk through an example trace for a p99 sample?
24:05 Priya: sure — here's a trace: 0-30ms request transfer, 30-110ms tokenization+prep, 110-250ms model forward (KV retrieval at 130ms), 250-380ms decode; tail cases show additional queuing 80-200ms before model forward. in ProviderX traces the KV hop added ~60-120ms.
24:30 Sandeep: that matches our ops traces.

27:40 Jordan: we also tried a smaller sequence packing strategy that reduced batch variance and improved p95 by ~15% while keeping p99 roughly same. packing helps when you have many short-turn requests.
27:55 Maya: interesting, we have mixed traffic with short and long; would you recommend sequence packing + routing?
28:02 Priya: yes, sequence packing for short-turns and routing long-turns to dedicated instances. helps keep both latency and cost efficient.

31:10 Tom: about logs and traces — we need request-level IDs in our APM, do you support correlation IDs?
31:16 Jordan: yes we pass through x-request-id by default and can add a per-token trace id in the private agent.

33:00 Maya: any security concerns with KV cache in-host? we store partial user context which is PHI in some prompts.
33:08 Jordan: for PHI you'd want Private deployment or Dedicated with encryption-at-rest and KMS. in-host KV in hosted offering is encrypted and after retention policy we purge, but enterprise PHI should be Private.
33:25 Sandeep: ok we will re-evaluate which traffic goes where.

35:10 Priya: next is tuning plan: 1) run mixed routing config with reserved pool for long seq; 2) q4 quant + eval tracking; 3) set autoscale thresholds tuned to your traffic percentiles; 4) run a CRC (customer-run-check) using 24hr of real traffic sample.
35:30 Maya: can Redwood help run the CRC on-prem? we prefer to keep data in our VPC.
35:37 Jordan: yes we support on-prem or VPC-private pilot; Priya can set up the perf harness for on-prem runs.

38:00 Tom: what about model parity — do we have exact model weights same as baseline? provider said they used a slightly newer fork which might explain differences.
38:08 Priya: we tried the same checkpoint you provided; provider fork may affect tokenization differences. we'll run a side-by-side with identical weights to ensure fair comparison.

41:20 Maya: okay next steps — walk through deliverables?
41:24 Jordan: sure — I'll send the benchmark spreadsheet, cost model, and pilot pricing by Monday (2026-06-22). Priya will push tuned configs and perf scripts by Wednesday (2026-06-24). Astra will upload the 24hr traffic sample and SLOs by Tuesday (2026-06-23). We'll schedule a deep dive to review traces on Friday (2026-06-26).
41:46 Maya: sounds good.

44:00 Sandeep: one last question on contract: if we move to Dedicated for long seq pool, can we do a 3-month reserved pilot?
44:07 Jordan: yes we have pilot reserved options, we'll include terms in the contract draft.

46:10 Jordan: all right thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links; Priya, any final notes?
46:16 Priya: just to emphasize, we'll run a fairness check for quality after quant and flag any regressions with example IDs.
46:24 Maya: perfect, thanks.
46:28 Jordan: endpoint — see you next week, we'll close action items and get the CRC started. bye.
46:35 (call ends)
